items.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: we had three bass players. They were all named John: it was John Heard, John Duke and John Clayton.

ctx.x: Yeah, the same people, and that worked out really good. But the Basie rhythm section, that’s one humongous responsibility to think about because, and I love being here with this jazz festival with John Heard because when I was on the band, four and a half years, we had three bass players. They were all named John: it was John Heard, John Duke and John Clayton. And John Heard left the band for a while and John Duke came in. John Duke left the band and John Heard came back. Then John left the band and Clayton came…

location in Chicago — checked into the hotel, had something to eat, met with Mr. Basie, and showed up for work. And that was it. Well you see, one of the wonderful things about something like that is that the leader of the band or the band itself will find out real fast if you can play, and real fast if you can’t. You know there’s no if. I mean you’re not hanging around for six months until someone says “well I don’t think he’s making it.” You know it’s phew, it’s real quick.
